as_read: Mixed: controlled exercise trials are mostly null, and cardiac trials are positive in patients at 15 g/day or more, far above most label servings.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: not named; repeated maximal exercise and muscle ATP recovery
studies_to_add.quote: Oral ribose supplementation with 4-g doses four times a day does not beneficially impact on postexercise muscle ATP recovery and maximal intermittent exercise performance.

studies_to_add.primary_endpoint: not named; anaerobic capacity and metabolic markers
studies_to_add.quote: Results indicate that oral ribose supplementation (10 g/d for 5 d) does not affect anaerobic exercise capacity or metabolic markers in trained subjects as evaluated in this study.

clinician_items: 24272966: dose-related falls in serum glucose up to 26.3 mg/dL (30.3% of baseline) in the first 60 minutes at 2.5 to 10 g, with an insulin response, in 12 healthy subjects. Relevant to anyone on glucose-lowering drugs.
36551203: narrative review warns of glycation capacity and predicted cytotoxicity of free ribose. Theoretical in the abstract, no clinical data given.
8815168: five McArdle's patients on 60 g/day reported disliking it; no harm stated in the abstract.
stored_rating_note: Stored positive_weak rests on one open-label uncontrolled pilot (17109576); the stored text says no placebo-controlled efficacy is established. It leaves out the controlled exercise trials and cardiac trials read here.
